references.text: Both tell of a barren woman who bears a son through God's intervention, where the name and upbringing mark the boy's special calling to the Lord's service.
Both women name their son as a testimony that the Lord has seen their distress and heard their prayer, even though the motives for the prayers vary.
Both tell of a barren woman who bears a son through God's intervention at a specific time, as an answer to a promise or prayer.
Both women name their son in response to the Lord having seen their distress, although Leah focuses on her husband's love and Hannah on God's answer.
Both sons receive names that directly mean 'God has heard,' and the birth is an answer to a woman's prayer or complaint to the Lord.
Both women name their son as a testimony that God has heard their voice and given them justice in their barrenness.
